title: Fluorescence Aggregation Imaging
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vzje74n

steps.title: Prepare imaging plates batch
steps.instruction: Pour a separate batch of imaging plates exactly seven days before each imaging day using 35 mm Petri dishes filled with 3.5 mL low‑peptone (0.013 % Difco Bacto) NGM agar (2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene); store the plates at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dry imaging plates
steps.instruction: Place the agar side down and dry the plates at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Seed bacterial lawn
steps.instruction: One to three hours before imaging, spot the centre of each plate with a single 20 µL drop of cold diluted OP50 (OD = 0.75) to create a uniform lawn.

steps.title: Synchronize hermaphrodites by bleach
steps.instruction: Bleach‑synchronize gravid hermaphrodites and keep them on a rotator at 20 °C until use.

steps.title: Re‑feed starved L1 worms
steps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, transfer starved L1 worms onto 3–4 culture plates (55 mm Petri dishes containing 15 mL low‑peptone (0.013 % Difco Bacto) NGM agar (2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene) seeded with OP50) and incubate at 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transfer starved L1 worms onto 3–4 culture plates with a glass pipette.

steps.title: Wash worms from culture plates
steps.instruction: Wash worms off the culture plates with M9 buffer, collect them in a 15 mL Falcon tube, perform two additional washes with M9, and aspirate as much supernatant as possible after the final wash. (Optional: for two‑colour imaging, mix 1–3 red‑marked worms with the 40 total worms during this stage.)

substeps.instruction: Wash worms off the culture plates with M9 buffer.
Collect the worms in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Wash the collected worms twice more with M9.
Aspirate as much supernatant as possible after the last wash.
Optional: mix 1–3 red‑marked worms with the 40 total worms for two‑colour imaging.

steps.title: Transfer worms to imaging plate
steps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, place exactly 40 worms in a small drop of M9 onto the imaging plate, positioning the drop away from the bacterial lawn.

steps.title: Vibrate plates to disperse worms
steps.instruction: After the M9 drop is absorbed, place the plate on a Vortex Genie 2 shaker (Scientific Industries) and vibrate at 600 rpm for 10 s to disburse worms and synchronize aggregation start across replicates.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Wait 20 s after vibration, then record for one hour on a Leica DMI6000 inverted microscope equipped with a 1.25× PL Fluotar objective (Leica), a TwinCam LS image splitter (Cairn) with dichroic cube (Cairn), and two Andor Zyla 5.5 cameras for simultaneous green‑red imaging. Illuminate continuously with blue (470 nm, 0.8 A) and green (cool white, 1.4 A) OptoLED (Cairn); acquire images as 100 ms exposures at 9 Hz using Andor Solis software v4.29.30005.0, saving as TIFF stacks. Keep the microscopy room at 21 °C throughout the recording.

steps.title: Compress and analyze image data
steps.instruction: Compress the TIFF image stacks and analyze them with Tierpsy Tracker software.
